commenti.body:
Agree! I even had some things spoiled via Twitter so I was like, well those must be the craziest parts. WRONG. And in any other movie some scenes could be accused of shock value just for the sake of it, but the story and characters warranted them all. 

Just such a fun movie.

>And in any other movie some scenes could be accused of shock value just for the sake of it, but the story and characters warranted them all. 

Exactly, for me, the scenes were making my mind switch from one decision to another, convincing me of one motive and then another scene saying: "you think you know but you have no clue".

I’ve seen a few people complain about the film being about ‘shock value’ and I understand why people might not personally be a fan of this sort of thing but I don’t think any of it was out of place with the overall tone + intention of the film.

Just saw it a couple of days ago and i haven’t stopped thinking about it. similarly i think attention to the form here really heightened enjoyment of the movie. maybe parts are surprising but honestly (i’m queer) i thought that was more than ok the movie has a heightened reality.

Really? I thought the movie was predictable. I figured out the “twist” that was going to happen towards the end of the film with his parents early  in the movie - the moment Oliver mentions his addict parents to Felix. It was kind of obvious considering the mood and character development.

Even the weird bath tub scene , what Oliver does there i predicted, maybe in a slightly different way than how it happened. It too was kind of obvious the moment they show the bath water being drained, camera lingering on the water, and Oliver staring into the door crack - right there, you kind of knew the ball park of what was going to happen next. 

And all the twists that follow were predictable. Overall, I didn’t like the movie. The only good thing was the beautiful visuals and memories of the city of Oxford where I once went on a day tour.
